gaps.sentence: There were ___ than twenty people at the meeting.
___ of what he says is nonsense.
gaps.explanation: 'Most of what he says' is the pattern 'most of + noun clause'; 'the most of' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: The hall was so crowded that ___ found a seat.
gaps.hint: a crowded hall means no one succeeded
gaps.explanation: 'So crowded that nobody found a seat' matches the logic of the sentence; 'anybody' cannot be the subject of an affirmative clause.

gaps.sentence: There weren't ___ chairs, so some guests had to stand.
gaps.explanation: 'Chairs' is countable and plural, so 'many' fits; 'much' and 'little' are for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: How ___ people came to the meeting?
gaps.explanation: 'Many' is used with countable plural nouns like people; 'much' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: There is ___ use asking him — he never checks his messages.
gaps.explanation: 'There is no use doing something' = it is pointless.

gaps.sentence: One of my shoes is tighter than ___.
gaps.hint: shoes come in pairs of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... than the other' is the pattern for two items; 'another' would suggest more than two.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.
